citations.authority: Defend Trade Secrets Act and Georgia Trade Secrets Act fee-shifting provisions
citations.citation_as_written: DTSA and Georgia Trade Secrets Act
citations.cited_for: Standards for recovery of attorneys' fees / fee-shifting
citations.context: Research standards for recovery of attorneys' fees in DTSA and Georgia Trade Secrets Act cases; prepare memorandum regarding fee-shifting provisions.

first_check.explanation: Both statutes contain fee-shifting provisions. Under the DTSA (§ 1836(b)(3)(D)), a court may award reasonable attorney's fees to the prevailing party for a bad-faith claim, a bad-faith motion about an injunction, or willful and malicious misappropriation. Under the GTSA (O.C.G.A. § 10-1-764), a court may award reasonable fees for willful and malicious misappropriation, as Brandenburg v. All-Fleet Refinishing confirms. The GTSA text itself could not be fetched because Justia returned a 403 error.
first_check.evidence_excerpt: § 1836(b)(3)(D): "the trade secret was willfully and maliciously misappropriated, award reasonable attorney's fees to the prevailing party"; Brandenburg: "OCGA § 10-1-764 provides that if the court finds wilful and malicious misappropriation, the court may award reasonable attorney fees to the prevailing party."
